answer: Reputation-gated task routing. Each identity's score is seeded by a one-time hardware-attested setup paid in a scarce resource (onyx-class metering credits), then routing priority scales with sustained accuracy across assigned jobs. Cloning forces the attacker to re-buy attestation and climb from zero score against an incumbent's order-of-magnitude head start, so parallel identities earn near-nothing until each independently passes a basalt-tier audit trail. The per-clone cost is the full attestation plus months of low-priority queue time on a shared knoll of throttled slots.
